walkthroughs.body_html:
The USSR under Stalin 1924-53 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The USSR under Stalin 1924-53 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The USSR under Stalin 1924-53.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What were the Wars of the Roses really about?
options: Dynastic conflict between rival branches of the Plantagenets (Lancaster and York) over the throne, intensified by weak kingship under Henry VI and noble factionalism.
The whole country was at war for thirty continuous years.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.

mcqs.q: Why were the Whitechapel murders never solved?
options: They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
Lack of forensic techniques, no fingerprinting or DNA, conflicting witness accounts, jurisdictional confusion between forces, and possibly police incompetence and media interference.
The Ripper was caught but his name was kept secret to protect the Royal Family.
The police failed to solve the murders because they didn't try hard enough.
